thread:
Omar Diaz: urgent help pls — my partner had a bad accident in Peru and they recommended air ambulance to Lima for surgery. Hospital did the transfer today and billed in PEN. I paid the provider locally. How do I file for emergency evacuation coverage and currency conversion? Don’t want to lose money on exchange.

Maya - People Ops: omg sorry to hear that, hope they’re ok. Quick steps: 1) upload all itemized invoices, receipts, and the transfer report to Benefits Portal > International Claims > Emergency. 2) include the clinical/medical necessity notes and facility contact. 3) keep original receipts (we need them for auditing). We can help with conversion and submitting to the carrier.

Omar Diaz: Uploaded: peru_air_amb_2026-07-12.pdf and hospital_receipt_surgery_pen.pdf. They show amounts in PEN and a receipt with the exchange rate used by the hospital.

Benefits Bot: Received emergency docs for Omar Diaz at 2026-07-12T14:03Z. Note: for foreign currency claims the carrier accepts either: a) hospital invoice + bank statement showing the card charge in USD, or b) official receipt + an independent FX conversion (OANDA/ECB) for the service date. For urgent requests mark "Expedite" in the portal to trigger same-day intake.

Claims Team: For air ambulance cases we often coordinate directly with the carrier's international desk. We can submit for reimbursement or direct-bill (if carrier will cover) but need: service dates, provider NPI/ID (or foreign equivalent), and proof of evacuation authorization if available. Omar, do you have the transfer authorization or a phone contact at the Peru facility?

Omar Diaz: I have a transfer report signed by the sending physician and the air-ambulance operator contact (phone + tax ID). Uploaded that too. No prior authorization was possible — it was emergent.

Maya - People Ops: Emergent transfers are covered under emergency services clause generally — carrier will evaluate clinical necessity. We'll attach the clinical notes and the air-ambulance operator invoice. For currency conversion, Claims Team will convert using OANDA rate on service date unless you provide a USD charge on your card. Which method did you use to pay?

Omar Diaz: Paid with my credit card and the statement shows two charges: PEN 48,000 (air ambulance) posted as USD 12,450 on my statement. Uploaded a redacted bank statement as proof.

Claims Team: Perfect — we'll use the bank-posted USD amount to avoid independent FX differences. Next steps: we submit to ZenithCare International Desk (claim type: Emergency Evacuation) with docs, flag for expedited review, and request direct payment to provider if carrier accepts. Typical turnaround 5-15 business days; expedited cases often faster.

Travel Support: If carrier denies direct payment, you’ll be reimbursed. For taxes/VAT paid locally, include the VAT line on the invoice — some carriers reimburse net of VAT depending on treaty. Also note: if you get any balance bills from the provider after insurer adjudication, upload them and we’ll assist appeals.

Maya - People Ops: Omar, Finance can help with an interim hardship reimbursement if you need cashflow before carrier processes. Ping me with the amount you paid and receipts. Also FYI — preserve copies of all ambulance logs and the transfer manifest; carriers request them for audit.

Omar Diaz: Thanks team. Submitted the hardship request for $12,450 and attached receipts. Appreciate the quick help.

Benefits Bot: Ticket created: INT-EMERG-2026-901. Claims assigned to caseworker Maria L. Estimated initial adjudication 7 business days.

Maya - People Ops: Following up here — we’ll keep the thread updated. Omar, please DM any sensitive IDs; don’t post them here. Sending best wishes to you and your partner.
